boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's os_mutex.c, 0x02058960..0x02058bb0: 8 functions, gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt. pret/pokediamond's arm9/lib/NitroSDK/src/OS_mutex.c defines, in this order, OS_InitMutex, OS_LockMutex, OS_UnlockMutex, OSi_UnlockAllMutex, OS_TryLockMutex, OSi_EnqueueTail and OSi_DequeueItem. All seven are here, each identified by body.

Order: mwccarm emits deferred bodies in reverse. The ROM run is pret's source order reversed, OSi_DequeueItem at 0x02058988 and OS_InitMutex highest. Below OSi_DequeueItem, func_02058960 unlinks the first mutex a thread holds (pret's OSi_RemoveMutexLinkFromQueue does this from OS_thread.c, taking the queue); here it takes the thread and is the file's last function.
TOP EDGE: DC_StoreAll (0x02058bb0) opens the cache primitives (arm9/CP15).
notes: Hand-assembled, following arm9/OS_Tick and arm9/OS_Alarm: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main.
The SDK names were given in this change (symbols/actor_renames.tsv records the evidence).
Text-only. OSMutex is this SDK's layout (a u16 thread queue) and stays local to the file: the callers (cstd4.cpp, cstd6.cpp, PM.cpp, OS_Thread.cpp) pass it as an opaque pointer.
